title: Kafka Event Streaming & Consumer Groups
subtitle: Append-only logs, ISR durability, partition offsets, backpressure & DLQs
overview: Apache Kafka decouples fast producers from slower downstream consumers using partitioned, immutable append-only logs. By preserving ordering within a partition key, using sequential disk I/O + zero-copy `sendfile`, and tracking consumer group offsets, Kafka sustains millions of events/sec with replayability.
firstPrinciplesStory: Checkout succeeds in Postgres, then calls Billing synchronously, then calls Email, then updates Analytics Search. Soon one slow Email provider stalls Checkout threads until customers double-click Pay. Worse, publishing to a naive in-memory queue deletes messages on delivery—so when an Analytics bug corrupts Tuesday's totals, yesterday's events are gone forever! Treating events as an immutable partitioned disk log (DDIA Ch. 11) gives you both real-time decoupling AND time-travel replay.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: A traditional queue is a whiteboard where each task gets erased as soon as a worker grabs it. Kafka is a ledger notebook with numbered pages divided into separate binders (partitions): Billing, Fraud, and Analytics can all read from the exact same immutable binder independently at their own reading speed using bookmarks (offsets).
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Producers hash partition keys (`order_id`) to route events into append-only partition segments flushed sequentially via OS page cache. `acks=all` commits once all In-Sync Replicas (`ISR`) persist the batch, advancing the High Watermark. Consumer groups assign 1 partition to at most 1 worker and commit offsets after idempotent writes.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: Never dual-write directly to Postgres and Kafka inside separate network calls—use the Transactional Outbox + CDC (DDIA Ch. 11) so DB state and event log never diverge. Also plan for poison-pill payloads via bounded retries + Dead-Letter Topics (`orders.dlq`), because blocking an infinite retry stalls every healthy message behind it in that partition. A DLQ is only safe as-is when events are independent: on a keyed, ordered stream, park the key so its later events wait behind the bad one.

ddiaAnchors.chapter: DDIA Ch. 11 · Stream Processing & Event Logs
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Retaining an immutable partitioned log allows multi-consumer fan-out, backpressure isolation, and deterministic replay.

pragmaticTips.tip: Design workflows so services interact through immutable events rather than synchronous temporal chains whenever immediate response isn't strictly required.
pragmaticTips.application: Emit `OrderPaid` once; let Billing, Notifications, and Search indexers evolve independently.

keyTakeaways: Strict message ordering is guaranteed ONLY within a single partition—choose partition keys carefully (e.g., `order_id` or `user_id`).
Set `acks=all` + `min.insync.replicas=2` for zero-data-loss durability on critical events.
Consumers must be idempotent because rebalance/crash recovery guarantees at-least-once delivery, not magic exactly-once across external DBs.

nodes.label: Checkout Producer
nodes.summary: Batches events per partition and waits for In-Sync Replica acknowledgment.
failureModes: Retry without enable.idempotence=true can duplicate messages in log

nodes.label: Kafka Partition 0 (Leader)
nodes.summary: Appends batches sequentially to OS page cache / segment file and replicates to ISR followers.
failureModes: Hot partition key concentrates all load onto one broker

nodes.label: ISR Follower Replica
nodes.summary: Continuously pulls batches from Partition Leader to stay inside In-Sync Replicas.
failureModes: Slow GC falls behind replica.lag.time.max.ms and drops out of ISR

nodes.label: Billing Consumer Group

specs.scalingAxis: Up to N consumers = N partitions

nodes.summary: Pulls records at its own pace (natural backpressure) and commits offset after idempotent DB upsert.
whenToUse: Independent consumer microservices reading the same event stream
failureModes: Max concurrency capped by partition count; poison pill blocks partition unless routed to DLQ

nodes.label: Dead-Letter Topic (DLQ)
nodes.summary: Quarantines malformed events after bounded retries so healthy messages keep flowing.
whenToUse: Preventing single corrupt schema payload from halting an entire partition
failureModes: Forgotten unmonitored DLQ silently drops business records

steps.payloadInspector: Batch { linger.ms: 5, compression: lz4, acks: all, idempotent: true }
steps.inspectorNote: Hashing by order_id pins every event for ord_7 to Partition 0, guaranteeing strict per-order ordering.

steps.info: Partition 0 Leader replicates offset 98413 to ISR Broker 2 -> High Watermark advances
steps.inspectorNote: Consumers can only read up to the High Watermark (fully replicated across ISR), preventing dirty reads on leader crash.

steps.info: Worker-0 pulls offset 98413, writes idempotent DB row, commits offset
steps.inspectorNote: Pull-based polling lets consumers absorb spikes safely—if Billing slows down, lag grows in Kafka instead of crashing Billing.

predictPrompt.prompt: Why must Billing's consumer write use `ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING` even when Kafka has `acks=all`?
predictPrompt.hint: Think about what happens if Billing updates Postgres and crashes 5ms BEFORE committing its Kafka offset.
predictPrompt.reveal: When the crashed consumer restarts or rebalances, Kafka redelivers from the last committed offset (at-least-once delivery). Making the consumer sink idempotent guarantees end-to-end effective-once state without brittle distributed 2PC transactions.

chaosScenarios.title: Poison-Pill Payload Quarantined to DLQ + Worker Crash Rebalance
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Offset 98415 (key ord_9, OrderCreated) contains a corrupted JSON payload that throws an unrecoverable schema exception.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: After 3 exponential retries, the consumer sends the event + stack trace to `orders.dlq` and parks key ord_9, so later ord_9 events are diverted behind it until it is fixed and replayed. Other keys keep flowing.

steps.info: DeserializationError on offset 98415 (attempt 3/3) -> Head-of-line partition block!
steps.inspectorNote: Without a DLQ, an unhandled exception crashes the worker in an infinite retry loop, stalling every order behind it.

steps.info: Published to orders.dlq with error headers; key ord_9 marked parked; Partition 0 offset committed to 98416
steps.payloadInspector: Topic: orders.dlq | x-original-offset: 98415 | x-error: SchemaMismatch | parked_keys += ord_9
steps.inspectorNote: Skipping 98415 is only safe when events are independent. On a keyed, ordered stream, applying ord_9's next event (say, a cancel) before its create breaks per-key order, so the key is parked instead.

steps.phaseTitle: 3. LATER EVENT FOR PARKED KEY DIVERTED
steps.info: Offset 98420 (key ord_9, OrderCancelled) -> ord_9 is parked -> appended to orders.dlq behind 98415
steps.payloadInspector: parked_keys lookup: ord_9 -> divert | ord_12, ord_13 ... -> process normally
steps.inspectorNote: On-call fixes 98415 and replays ord_9's parked events in order, then un-parks the key. Healthy orders never waited.

pros: Durable replayable history for multiple consumer groups
cons: Max active workers per group bounded by partition count
tradeoffs.bestFor: Event sourcing, analytics pipelines, CDC, multi-consumer domain events

cons: Messages deleted after ack (no time-travel replay)
tradeoffs.bestFor: Background task queues (emails, PDF generation, video job dispatch)
